hero.headline: House Republicans advance framework for third budget reconciliation bill
hero.body:
Senate Republicans approved a budget resolution Thursday that would allocate up to $140 billion to immigration enforcement agencies, advancing a third major budget reconciliation bill as the party pursues its legislative priorities. The measure passed along nearly party lines in an early morning vote, setting the stage for the House to consider similar legislation.

The budget resolution passed 50-48, with all Democrats opposed. Two Republicans, Lisa Murkowski of Alaska and Rand Paul of Kentucky, also voted against the measure. The approval marks a critical step in the reconciliation process, which allows certain bills to pass the Senate with a simple majority rather than the usual 60-vote threshold.

The funding would go to Immigration and Customs Enforcement and Customs and Border Protection, two agencies that have operated without money since mid-February when the Department of Homeland Security began a partial shutdown. Senate Republican Majority Leader John Thune said the resolution represents progress toward ending the shutdown while securing border operations.

"We have a multi-step process ahead of us, but at the end Republicans will have helped ensure that America's borders are secure and prevented Democrats from defunding these important agencies," Thune said.

Democrats have opposed funding these agencies following the deaths of two U.S. citizens in January during an intensive immigration operation in Minneapolis. After weeks of negotiations with the Trump administration, Democrats sought reforms including restrictions on federal agents wearing masks during operations and requirements for warrants before stopping people. Those talks ultimately broke down, prompting Republicans to move forward unilaterally through reconciliation.

House Speaker Mike Johnson indicated he would schedule a separate vote on bipartisan DHS funding legislation previously approved by the Senate, but only after progress is made on the reconciliation bill. "Sequencing is important. We have to make sure we don't isolate and make an orphan out of key agencies of the department," Johnson said.

Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer criticized the Republican approach, saying the funding allocation reflects misplaced priorities. "Tonight, Senate Republicans showed the American people where they stand: not for families struggling with the high costs of childcare, groceries and gasoline, electricity, but for pumping $140bn towards rogue agencies," Schumer said after the vote.

During the amendment process known as "vote-a-rama," Democrats proposed changes focused on affordability concerns, including amendments addressing grocery prices and out-of-pocket healthcare costs. Senators Susan Collins of Maine and Dan Sullivan of Alaska, both considered vulnerable in upcoming elections, voted in favor of those amendments, though they did not advance.

The House must now adopt the budget resolution before committees can proceed with writing specific legislation to unlock the funding for the two agencies.

cards.headline: Trump says Iran peace deal could be reached within days
cards.body:
President Trump announced he could approve an Iran peace deal on Friday that would require major concessions from Tehran, including opening the strait of Hormuz and eliminating the country's nuclear programme. However, top Iranian officials disputed his claims, signalling that no final agreement had been reached.

Trump spent more than two hours in the White House situation room with senior aides before making his announcement. On his Truth Social platform, he outlined the terms he said Iran must accept: never developing nuclear weapons, opening the strait of Hormuz to all traffic without tolls, removing mines from the waterway, and allowing the US to collect and destroy highly enriched uranium from an Iranian nuclear site. Trump also said he would lift the US naval blockade against Iran, though it remained unclear whether this would be contingent on the agreement being confirmed.

The list of demands presented by Trump as a completed agreement would indicate Iran had capitulated on key positions, including its historical right to collect tolls from ships using the strait, the release of frozen assets, and its insistence on maintaining its nuclear programme.

Iranian officials quickly rejected Trump's characterisation of the negotiations. The semi-official Tasnim news agency reported that no final understanding had been reached and described Trump's post as "in line with his usual pattern of making unilateral and egotistical statements." Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei told state media that "exchanges of messages are continuing, but no final agreement has been reached yet."

Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said discussions about the strait of Hormuz had focused on management "in line with our sovereign responsibilities and international law," suggesting Iran would not accept Trump's proposed terms. Iran's Fars news agency characterised Trump's announcement as a "mixture of truth and lies" that did not reflect actual negotiations.

A White House official confirmed the situation room meeting had lasted approximately two hours but did not announce a deal. The official stated: "President Trump will only make a deal that is good for America and satisfies his red lines. Iran can never possess a nuclear weapon."

Iran's top negotiator Mohammad-Bagher Ghalibaf sent a defiant message, declaring that Iran had "no trust in guarantees or words, only actions are the measure." He suggested Iran was prepared to resume fighting if talks failed to extend the ceasefire and end the war.

A meeting in Washington between US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Pakistan's Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, who serves as a key mediator, ended without public comment on the negotiations. Trump reportedly needed more time to decide whether to accept a negotiated agreement that would defer difficult issues, including the fate of Iran's remaining nuclear material stockpile, into subsequent negotiations.

cards.headline: Israel Strikes Southern Lebanon After Cease-Fire Falters
cards.teaser: Israeli forces conducted new strikes in southern Lebanon, complicating US-Iran peace negotiations.
cards.body:
Israel launched fresh attacks across southern Lebanon on Friday, targeting what it described as Hezbollah positions, just one day after a US-brokered ceasefire proposal collapsed. The strikes came after Hezbollah rejected a deal that would have required the militant group to stop firing while allowing Israel to continue its military operations.

The Israeli military issued forced evacuation orders for nine villages in southern Lebanon before the bombardment began. Thousands of residents fled their homes, with hundreds of families leaving Anqoun, a village sheltering at least 2,500 displaced people. Roads to Sidon, the nearest large city, became congested with cars as families sought safety.

Israeli forces carried out extensive airstrikes and artillery strikes across the region, including drone strikes on vehicles in the Nabatieh area and attacks on the town of Kfar Tebnit. The strikes occurred as Israeli troops deepened their invasion further south, with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordering the military to advance after capturing Beaufort Castle, a medieval crusader fortress, earlier in the week.

Hezbollah responded to the Israeli military presence near the castle with rocket barrages targeting Israeli troops. The fighting underscored the fragility of ceasefire efforts and the challenges of negotiating without the militant group's direct participation.

The proposed ceasefire, which Israel and Lebanon's government had discussed, was rejected by Hezbollah as tantamount to surrender. Hezbollah is not a party to the negotiations between Israel and Lebanon's government. Instead, the group communicates through Lebanon's parliament speaker, Nabih Berri, who had previously suggested Hezbollah would stop firing if fighting ceased entirely.

On Friday, Berri stated that Hezbollah would only withdraw from the area south of the Litani River, about 18 miles from the Lebanon-Israel border, if Israeli troops withdrew from Lebanon and a ceasefire was truly unconditional. He also criticized provisions allowing Israeli forces to maintain presence in certain "pilot zones" while Lebanese troops returned to other areas.

Israel currently occupies more than 608 square kilometers of Lebanese territory. On Thursday, Israeli forces withdrew from the town of Dibbin, marking the first pullback since fighting began on March 2. Lebanese troops and UN peacekeepers entered the town on Friday.

Netanyahu told ministers he would not seek cabinet approval for the ceasefire unless Hezbollah first agreed to its terms. Several ministers opposed the fragile arrangement, but Netanyahu refused their demands for a formal vote, saying there was no deal to approve until Hezbollah endorsed it.

The conflict has caused significant casualties. More than 3,500 people have been killed by Israeli strikes in Lebanon, while Hezbollah has killed at least 29 Israeli soldiers and three Israeli civilians in the country.

The Lebanese prime minister, Nawaf Salam, expressed frustration with the ongoing conflict, stating that Lebanon cannot continue to be a battleground for wars fought by other nations.

cards.headline: Oil Prices Fall After Israel and Iran Agree to Halt Strikes
cards.teaser: Oil prices declined following an agreement between Israel and Iran to cease strikes against each other.
cards.body:
Oil prices dropped after Israel and Iran reached an agreement to halt military strikes against one another, reducing fears of a broader regional conflict. The brief escalation had driven crude prices higher as markets priced in potential supply disruptions from the Persian Gulf region.

The ceasefire agreement eases immediate concerns about attacks on energy infrastructure or shipping routes that could affect global oil supplies. Energy markets had reacted sharply to the conflict, with traders monitoring any signs that hostilities could spread or threaten production facilities in the region.

cards.headline: US Missile Strikes Oil Tanker Off Oman, Crew Calls for Help
cards.teaser: A US missile struck a sanctioned oil tanker off the coast of Oman on Monday, leaving the vessel on fire and sinking as its Indian crew issued urgent distress ca.
cards.body:
A US missile hit a sanctioned oil tanker off the coast of Oman on Monday, setting the vessel ablaze. The Indian crew broadcast distress calls asking for help as the ship caught fire and began sinking in waters near the Strait of Hormuz.

In a separate incident the same day, an Apache helicopter went down in the region. An uncrewed vessel rescued the two crew members from the downed aircraft, according to US officials.

cards.headline: Sea drone rescues crew after US Apache helicopter crashes near Strait of Hormuz
cards.teaser: An uncrewed vessel retrieved two crew members after their Apache helicopter went down, marking the first rescue of its kind.
cards.body:
An Apache helicopter crashed near the Strait of Hormuz on Monday, with two crew members on board. An uncrewed sea vessel responded to the incident and successfully rescued both individuals from the water.

The rescue marked the first time an autonomous sea drone has been used to recover personnel from a downed aircraft, according to US officials.

cards.headline: Pentagon Adds Alibaba and Baidu to List of Companies Aiding Chinese Military
cards.body:
The Pentagon has expanded its roster of Chinese companies accused of supporting Beijing's military operations, adding major tech firms Alibaba and Baidu along with several others. The designation prevents these companies from receiving U.S. defense contracts and represents another step in Washington's campaign to restrict Chinese access to American technology and markets.

The updated list, released on Monday, includes e-commerce giant Alibaba, search engine provider Baidu, biotechnology firm WuXi AppTec, electric vehicle manufacturer BYD, and robotics company Unitree. The Pentagon's assessment suggests these companies possess technologies or provide services with potential applications for enhancing Chinese military capabilities.

Alibaba operates one of the world's largest e-commerce platforms and a significant cloud computing business. Baidu leads the Chinese internet search market and has invested heavily in artificial intelligence and autonomous driving development. WuXi AppTec provides drug development services to pharmaceutical companies globally. BYD ranks among the world's largest electric vehicle manufacturers.

The Pentagon's determination carries restrictions on defense contracting but does not impose the broader investment prohibitions associated with Treasury Department sanctions. The financial impact on these companies varies based on their existing exposure to U.S. defense contracts. For consumer-focused firms like Alibaba and Baidu, such contracts have historically been minimal. However, the designation creates reputational risks and may influence decisions by other Western governments and companies regarding partnerships and procurement.

The announcement comes less than a month after Donald Trump met with China's Xi Jinping in Beijing, where the two leaders worked to maintain a fragile trade war truce. The timing of the expanded list could complicate diplomatic efforts between the countries.

The Trump administration had initially released an updated version of the list four months earlier, according to reporting, but then withdrew it without explanation before the current release.

U.S. officials have increasingly examined Chinese technology companies amid concerns about data security, supply chain vulnerabilities, and the relationship between private enterprise and state interests under Chinese law. Previous designations have targeted telecommunications equipment makers, surveillance technology firms, and semiconductor companies.

Chinese officials have previously characterized such measures as economic coercion and pledged to protect the interests of Chinese businesses operating globally. The move adds to broader tensions between Washington and Beijing, undermining recent diplomatic initiatives aimed at stabilizing the relationship.

The Pentagon's determination reflects growing American concerns about the scope of civilian Chinese companies allegedly contributing to military modernization efforts.

cards.headline: US Army Helicopter Crew Rescued by Sea Drone Near Strait of Hormuz
cards.teaser: An uncrewed vessel retrieved two crew members after their Apache helicopter went down in Gulf waters.
cards.body:
Two crew members of a US Army Apache helicopter were rescued by an uncrewed sea vessel after their aircraft crashed near the Strait of Hormuz on Monday. President Trump confirmed that both pilots were safe following the incident.

The rescue marked an unusual application of drone technology for search and rescue operations in the strategically important waterway, where US military activity has been elevated in recent days.

cards.headline: Stray Drones From Ukraine War Threaten Neighboring Countries
cards.teaser: Unmanned aircraft launched by both Russia and Ukraine are veering off course into countries not involved in the conflict.
cards.body:
Drones deployed by both Russian and Ukrainian forces in their ongoing war are increasingly straying into the airspace of neighboring countries, creating security concerns for nations not party to the conflict. The errant unmanned aircraft have forced regional governments to address the unexpected spillover effects of drone warfare.

The incidents highlight the challenges of controlling autonomous and remotely piloted aircraft in active combat zones, particularly when flight paths take them near international borders. Countries bordering Ukraine have expressed growing alarm as the frequency of drone incursions has increased.

cards.headline: Kenyan Police Use Tear Gas on Protesters Opposing US Ebola Center
cards.teaser: Demonstrators in Kenya rallied against a proposed American quarantine facility for Ebola treatment.
cards.body:
Kenyan police used tear gas to disperse protesters opposing the construction of a US-funded Ebola quarantine and treatment centre. The demonstrators raised concerns about potential cross-border infection risks and expressed frustration over insufficient government transparency regarding the facility's plans and operations.

The proposed centre has become a contentious issue, with local communities questioning whether authorities adequately consulted with them about the project and its safety implications for the region.

cards.headline: Iran Loses World Cup Ticket Allocation Days Before Tournament
cards.teaser: Iranian football federation says its group stage tickets were revoked ahead of the tournament's start.
cards.body:
Iran's football federation announced that its ticket allocation for the World Cup has been revoked just days before the tournament begins. The federation had already started selling tickets to fans for matches scheduled in Los Angeles and Seattle but can no longer provide them.

The revocation leaves Iranian supporters who made travel plans unable to attend their team's group stage matches against New Zealand, Belgium, and Egypt. The federation said the decision "raises questions about interference of non-sporting considerations," suggesting the move involved factors beyond the sport itself.

cards.headline: Man Arrested After Stabbing Attack in Belfast
cards.teaser: Northern Ireland police detained a suspect following what officials described as a brutal knife attack.
cards.body:
A man was arrested on suspicion of attempted murder following a stabbing incident in Belfast that left one person seriously injured. Police described the knife attack as brutal and barbaric. Prime Minister Keir Starmer called the attack sickening.

Authorities responded swiftly to apprehend a suspect as they investigated the circumstances of the assault. Police and British politicians appealed for calm following the incident.

cards.headline: Los Angeles councilmember Nithya Raman advances to mayoral runoff
cards.teaser: Raman will face incumbent Mayor Karen Bass in a runoff election after overtaking a Republican challenger for second place.
cards.body:
Nithya Raman, a progressive Los Angeles city council member, has advanced to the November mayoral runoff after edging out Spencer Pratt. The former reality TV star had initially held a lead following last week's election, but Raman pulled ahead as ballot processing continued.

Raman will face incumbent Mayor Karen Bass in the runoff to lead the second largest city in the United States. Pratt decided to run for mayor after his Pacific Palisades home burned down in the 2025 wildfires.

cards.headline: Four states hold primary elections
cards.teaser: Voters in four states are casting ballots in primary elections to select candidates for upcoming races.
cards.body:
Primary elections are underway in four states as voters select candidates who will compete in general elections. The contests include races at various levels of government, from local offices to congressional seats.

The primaries represent key steps in the electoral process as parties finalize their candidates ahead of the general election season. Results from these contests will shape the political landscape and determine which candidates advance to face voters in November.

cards.headline: Teacher and two students stabbed at Manchester school
cards.teaser: A knife attack at Co-op Academy in Blackley left three people injured, and police arrested a 14-year-old girl.
cards.body:
A teacher and two students were stabbed during an attack at Co-op Academy in Blackley, Manchester. Police responded to the incident and took a 14-year-old schoolgirl into custody in connection with the assault.

Authorities have not released information about the condition of the injured individuals or details about what preceded the attack. The incident occurred at the school, prompting an emergency response from local law enforcement and medical services.

cards.headline: Man sentenced in first prosecution for sex-based harassment
cards.teaser: David Stroud was convicted in May for grabbing a woman's hair and asking for a kiss in a legal first.
cards.body:
David Stroud has been sentenced following his May conviction for grabbing a woman's hair and asking for a kiss. The case marked the first prosecution of its kind for sex-based harassment under new legal standards.

Prosecutors described the conviction as a landmark case that established new precedent for addressing street harassment. The guilty verdict represents an expansion of how harassment laws are applied in cases involving physical contact and unwanted advances.

cards.headline: Man jailed for murdering partner and setting fire to home
cards.teaser: Clifton George stabbed Annabel Rook 31 times before starting a fire at their house in north London.
cards.body:
Clifton George has been sentenced to prison for murdering his partner Annabel Rook at their home in Stoke Newington, north London. George stabbed Rook 31 times after she attempted to end their relationship, then set fire to their house.

Rook's friends said the killing demonstrated that domestic violence can affect anyone. The case highlighted the dangers faced by individuals trying to leave abusive relationships, as Rook was killed when she tried to separate from George.

cards.headline: OpenAI Plans Stock Offering Amid Questions About Market Capacity
cards.teaser: OpenAI is testing investor appetite for a major initial public offering alongside planned offerings from SpaceX and Anthropic.
cards.body:
OpenAI has filed confidentially to go public on the US stock market, positioning itself for one of the most highly valued listings in market history with an expected valuation exceeding $850 billion. The company announced the filing publicly, noting that it expects details to leak anyway.

OpenAI has not yet decided on timing for the public offering, suggesting it may remain private for some time. The company indicated there are strategic advantages to staying private currently, though going public remains an option depending on how circumstances evolve.

cards.headline: U.S. Exports Rose in April as War Boosted Oil Demand
cards.teaser: Commerce Department data showed U.S. exports increased in April, slightly outpacing import growth.
cards.body:
U.S. exports grew in April, with the increase slightly exceeding the growth in imports, according to Commerce Department data. The war with Iran contributed to higher oil demand, supporting export activity during the month.

The trade figures reflect shifting patterns in global commerce as geopolitical tensions affect energy markets and commodity flows. The modest improvement in the export-import balance comes as the U.S. economy navigates the economic consequences of ongoing military operations.

cards.headline: Apple Delays Siri AI Upgrade in Europe Over Regulatory Dispute
cards.teaser: A regulatory disagreement has indefinitely postponed the release of Apple's artificial intelligence upgrade for Siri in Europe.
cards.body:
Apple announced a major upgrade to Siri at its developer conference, integrating it with Apple Intelligence to create a more advanced voice assistant similar to ChatGPT or Google Gemini. The enhanced Siri is scheduled for a broad rollout in fall.

However, the upgrade will not be available in Europe due to a regulatory dispute. The delay leaves European users without access to the new AI-powered features while customers in other markets receive the enhanced voice assistant.

cards.headline: Stock Futures Rise as Oil Falls and Chip Stocks Rebound
cards.teaser: U.S. stock futures pointed higher as oil prices declined and semiconductor stocks continued recovering.
cards.body:
U.S. stock futures climbed as oil prices fell following a ceasefire agreement between Iran and Israel. Semiconductor stocks extended gains as investors regained confidence in the technology sector, with Nasdaq futures pointing to further recovery after recent market turbulence.

The easing of Middle East tensions helped stabilize crude prices after earlier volatility. Chip stocks bounced back as the AI trade resumed momentum, supported by renewed investor appetite for the sector heading into the market open.

cards.headline: Dubai Faces Economic Pressure as Conflict Disrupts Trade and Travel
cards.teaser: Dubai's economy is being tested as the war with Iran affects the city's trade and travel sectors.
cards.body:
Dubai's economy is being tested as conflict in the Persian Gulf threatens the trade and travel sectors that underpin its prosperity. The emirate has long served as a regional hub for international commerce and tourism, relying on stable shipping routes and air connections.

Oil prices fell after Israel and Iran agreed to halt strikes against each other, easing concerns about broader regional escalation. However, uncertainty remains for businesses dependent on the stability of Gulf trade corridors and Dubai's position as a safe destination for international business and leisure travel.

hero.headline: Apple announces third generation foundation models and new AI features at WWDC
hero.body:
Apple unveiled its third generation of foundation models and introduced a revamped artificial intelligence system for Siri at its Worldwide Developers Conference. The company presented iOS 27 and detailed how its AI capabilities, branded as Apple Intelligence, will function across its device ecosystem with new features designed to make Siri more conversational and capable.

The updated Siri will resemble AI chatbots like ChatGPT or Google Gemini more closely than a traditional question-and-answer tool drawing from the web. The voice assistant will be widely released in the fall as part of a major upgrade that comes after years of user frustration and false starts.

Apple's announcement addresses concerns about the company falling behind competitors in the artificial intelligence race. Industry observers noted that while Apple's technology appears capable, the delayed timeline means the company is entering a market where other tech firms have already established their AI offerings. The company emphasized that its focus has been on building AI that prioritizes user privacy and integrates seamlessly with its hardware and software ecosystem.

A notable aspect of Apple's approach involves running some AI models on servers operated by Google, while maintaining user privacy commitments. According to Apple, even when processing occurs on Google's cloud infrastructure, Google does not have any kind of access to user data or queries. This hybrid approach allows Apple to offer more powerful AI features that require server-side processing while keeping its privacy promises.

Tim Cook highlighted the AI-forward upgrade during what was described as his final WWDC keynote. The presentation emphasized the many improvements being tackled alongside the Siri enhancement, presenting Apple's AI strategy as a comprehensive effort across the company's product line.

The announcement comes after the company reached a 250 million dollar settlement related to false advertising, with observers noting that the vibe of Apple's 2026 WWDC keynote felt like a company listing accomplishments proudly. One subtle aspect included the many AI demonstrations of someone standing with phone in hand.

Apple also announced new child safety features for iPhones and iPads alongside the Siri upgrades, indicating a broader approach to AI integration that extends beyond voice assistant improvements.

The new features will be available in iOS 27 when it launches later this year. Apple did not provide a specific release date but typically makes new iOS versions available in the fall. Notably, some AI features will not be available in Europe initially, though specific reasons for the regional limitation were not detailed at the conference.

cards.headline: NASA to announce astronauts selected for Artemis III moon mission
cards.teaser: The space agency will unveil the crew for its planned lunar landing mission and provide updates on the broader Artemis program.
cards.body:
NASA plans to reveal the names of astronauts selected to fly on the Artemis III mission, which aims to return humans to the lunar surface. The announcement will include updates on the overall Artemis program timeline and mission objectives.

The Artemis III mission is designed to land astronauts on the moon for the first time since the Apollo program ended in the 1970s. NASA has maintained a shortlist of astronauts eligible for the mission, drawn from its current astronaut corps. The selection represents a significant milestone in the agency's plans to establish a sustained presence on and around the moon.

cards.headline: Researchers find large fan-shaped geological structure beneath Antarctic ice
cards.teaser: Scientists discovered a vast subglacial formation in East Antarctica created by rotational extension processes.
cards.body:
A team of geoscientists identified a previously unknown fan-shaped structure beneath the ice sheet in East Antarctica. The formation, described as a subglacial basin province, was created through rotational extension, a geological process that shapes the Earth's crust.

The discovery was published in the journal Nature and represents a significant finding for understanding the geological history and structure of the Antarctic continent. The formation spans a large area beneath the ice and provides new insights into the tectonic forces that have shaped the region over millions of years.

cards.headline: Jupiter and Venus appear close together in rare planetary conjunction
cards.teaser: The two brightest planets in the night sky will be visible in close proximity, creating a striking celestial display.
cards.body:
Jupiter and Venus are meeting in a conjunction visible to observers around the world. The two planets will appear extremely close together in the night sky, an event sometimes described as the planets appearing to kiss due to their proximity from Earth's perspective.

The conjunction occurs when the orbital paths of the two planets align from Earth's viewpoint, making them appear near each other despite being millions of miles apart in space. Venus and Jupiter are the two brightest planets visible from Earth, making this conjunction particularly striking. The event is visible without specialized equipment, though binoculars or telescopes can enhance the view.

cards.headline: Rivian releases R2 electric vehicle priced below $60,000
cards.teaser: The automaker's second electric vehicle model aims to bring its technology to a broader market with a more accessible price point.
cards.body:
Rivian's second electric vehicle, the R2, marks the company's entry into the mainstream EV market with a starting price under $60,000. After building cult status with its pricier R1S SUV and R1T pickup, Rivian is now targeting broader appeal with the 2027 model year R2.

Early test drives reveal a vehicle that balances key features from Rivian's existing lineup while delivering an engaging driving experience. The R2 represents a critical next step for the company as it pursues mainstream market success beyond its premium segment origins.

cards.headline: Lovable reports $500 million in annualized revenue with one million weekly projects
cards.teaser: The software platform says users are building businesses and replacing internal systems using its tools.
cards.body:
Lovable has surpassed $500 million in annualized run-rate revenue, with users creating one million new projects each week on the platform. The no-code software company enables developers to build applications without traditional programming, and its user base is increasingly deploying these tools for production systems and real businesses.

The growth reflects a shift beyond experimental use cases, as organizations leverage Lovable to create new business solutions and replace legacy internal software systems. The scale of weekly project creation demonstrates strong adoption momentum across the platform.

cards.headline: Sandstone secures $30 million Series A for AI legal software
cards.teaser: The startup is developing artificial intelligence tools designed for in-house legal departments.
cards.body:
Sandstone raised $30 million in Series A funding led by Lightspeed Partners, with participation from Sequoia. The company builds AI-powered software for in-house legal teams at corporations.

The funding reflects growing investor confidence in AI applications within the legal sector. Sandstone is targeting corporate legal departments specifically, rather than law firms or litigation practices. The company plans to use the capital to develop its product and expand its team.

hero.headline: Browns guard Joel Bitonio retires after 12 seasons
hero.body:
Cleveland Browns guard Joel Bitonio announced his retirement after 12 seasons with the team. The seven-time Pro Bowl selection and two-time All-Pro spent his entire NFL career with Cleveland after the team selected him in the second round of the 2014 draft.

Bitonio became one of the most consistent offensive linemen in franchise history, earning Pro Bowl honors in seven of his 12 seasons. He was named first-team All-Pro twice during his career. The guard started 179 games for the Browns, providing stability on the offensive line through multiple coaching changes and quarterback transitions.

The Nevada product was part of the Browns' offensive line during the team's playoff appearances in recent years. He played a key role in protecting the quarterback and opening running lanes as Cleveland worked to rebuild its roster. His durability and performance made him one of the few constants during a period of significant roster turnover for the franchise.

Bitonio's retirement removes a veteran presence from the Browns' offensive line heading into the upcoming season. The team will need to find a replacement for one of the most decorated players in recent franchise history. His departure marks the end of an era for Cleveland's offensive line, which will undergo significant changes without the longtime starter.

The announcement comes during the offseason as teams prepare for training camp. Bitonio's decision to retire now gives the Browns time to evaluate their options at the guard position before the start of the season.

cards.headline: Iran's World Cup ticket allocation revoked days before tournament
cards.teaser: Iran's football federation says its ticket allocation for the group stage has been withdrawn just days before the World Cup begins.
cards.body:
Iran's football federation announced that its ticket allocation for the World Cup group stage has been revoked just days before the tournament begins. The decision leaves Iranian supporters unable to attend matches despite having already made travel arrangements and begun the ticket purchasing process.

Iran is scheduled to play three group matches: against New Zealand and Belgium in Los Angeles on June 15 and 21 respectively, and against Egypt in Seattle on June 26. The federation stated the revocation "raises questions about interference of non-sporting considerations" in its statement.

cards.headline: Somali referee denied US entry for World Cup
cards.teaser: Referee Omar Artan says he was subjected to an 11-hour immigration interview before being denied entry to the United States despite holding valid documents.
cards.body:
Omar Artan, a top African referee, has been denied entry to the United States and will miss the 2026 World Cup. He was set to become the first Somali to officiate at a World Cup.

FIFA confirmed that Artan "will be unable to train and officiate at the FIFA World Cup 2026" and stated that US authorities informed them his status would not change. The governing body deferred responsibility to the US government for the decision.

cards.headline: Big Ten to discuss Texas Tech scheduling ban over gambling ruling
cards.teaser: The Big Ten will discuss a mandate to prohibit member schools from scheduling Texas Tech in any sport following a court ruling about quarterback Brendan Sorsby.
cards.body:
The Big Ten conference plans to discuss implementing a league-wide ban on scheduling Texas Tech across all sports. The potential mandate stems from a court ruling related to Texas Tech quarterback Brendan Sorsby's gambling ban, which was overturned by a court.

The NCAA has appealed the court ruling that overturned Sorsby's gambling ban. The case has raised questions about the NCAA's ability to enforce its rules through the court system and whether other conferences or organizations should take independent action.

cards.headline: Former UEFA president Platini files legal action against FIFA
cards.teaser: Michel Platini initiated civil and legal proceedings against FIFA and current president Gianni Infantino over corruption allegations from 2015.
cards.body:
Former UEFA president Michel Platini has initiated civil and legal proceedings against FIFA and its president Gianni Infantino. The action concerns corruption allegations that date back to 2015.

Platini's legal challenge represents his effort to contest the allegations through the courts. The proceedings mark a significant development in a long-running controversy that previously engulfed FIFA leadership.

cards.headline: Raducanu wins opening match at Queen's Club
cards.teaser: Emma Raducanu began her Wimbledon preparations with a straight-set victory over Anna Blinkova in a rain-disrupted match.
cards.body:
Emma Raducanu opened her grass-court season with a straight-set victory over Anna Blinkova at Queen's Club. The match was disrupted by rain but Raducanu completed the win to start her Wimbledon preparations on a positive note.

The British player is using the Queen's Club tournament to prepare for Wimbledon, which begins later this month. The victory marks a promising start to her grass-court campaign after the previous hard-court season.

cards.headline: England rests Itoje for training camp, calls up Elliott
cards.teaser: Saracens wing Tobias Elliott is among the prospects called up for an England training camp this week as the team rests Maro Itoje.
cards.body:
England has called up Saracens wing Tobias Elliott for a small-scale training camp this week as part of the squad preparation ahead of a fixture between an England XV and France XV in Vanns on Friday week.

Captain Maro Itoje has been left out of the 26-player squad and is expected to be rested ahead of the summer tour. England hopes to give Itoje a break unless injuries to other second row options force a change in plans. Other senior players including Jamie George, Ben Earl and Tom Curry are involved in the camp, alongside uncapped prospects such as Gloucester's Afolabi Fasogbon and Bristol's Benhard Janse van Rensburg.

hero.headline: Ariana Grande and Ethan Slater Split After Three Years Together
hero.body:
Singer Ariana Grande and actor Ethan Slater have ended their relationship after nearly three years of dating. The separation occurred several months ago, though the couple kept the news private until recently.

Grande, 32, and Slater, 32, began dating in 2023 after meeting on the set of the Wicked film adaptation, where Grande plays Glinda and Slater portrays Boq. Both were navigating the end of previous relationships when their romance began. Grande had been married to real estate agent Dalton Gomez, while Slater was separating from his high school sweetheart Lilly Jay, with whom he shares a young son.

From the start, their relationship attracted significant public attention. However, the couple maintained a largely private partnership, rarely appearing together publicly and seldom discussing their romance in interviews. Despite the scrutiny, sources indicated they remained committed to their relationship while managing demanding careers and personal responsibilities.

Grande has channeled energy into her music career and Wicked promotion. The film has become a major box office success, earning 765 million dollars worldwide and winning two Oscars. Slater, who received a Tony nomination for his performance in the Broadway musical SpongeBob SquarePants, has continued working in theater and film. The pressures of their respective professional commitments reportedly created strain in maintaining their relationship.

Neither Grande nor Slater has publicly addressed the split. Their representatives have declined to comment on details surrounding the separation or their current personal circumstances. Grande maintains an active social media presence but has not discussed the breakup with her followers.

The split comes approximately a year after the Wicked: For Good premiere, which was marked by a notable incident at the Singapore premiere. During a red carpet event, a barrier breach led to a security situation involving Grande and her co-star Cynthia Erivo. Erivo later discussed the incident in interviews, describing the moment as frightening for both performers.

Erivo reflected on public reactions to the incident, noting that she felt responses reflected broader issues regarding perception and assumptions. She explained that she had moved instinctively to assist Grande when a stranger breached security protocols. Erivo described feeling that her actions had been mischaracterized based on appearance and expressed concern about how the situation was interpreted on social media.

The Wicked sequel has performed differently than the first film at the box office, taking 541 million dollars worldwide, and did not receive Oscar nominations.

cards.headline: Katy Perry Calls Justin Trudeau 'Love of My Life' at Public Appearance
cards.teaser: Singer Katy Perry publicly celebrated her relationship with former Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau, marking a major milestone for the couple.
cards.body:
Katy Perry referred to boyfriend Justin Trudeau as the "love of my life" during a recent public appearance. The couple made their red carpet debut at the Tribeca Festival, signaling a new level of openness about their relationship.

Trudeau reportedly wants Perry to live part of the year at his $3.1 million Canada home with their blended family. The couple was seen dancing together during a date night, with Perry describing herself as "very in love." The relationship marks a significant personal chapter for both the pop star and the former political leader.

cards.headline: U.K. Regulators Launch Investigation Into Paramount-Warner Bros. Merger
cards.teaser: The Competition and Markets Authority has opened a formal investigation into the proposed $110 billion acquisition combining two major entertainment companies.
cards.body:
The U.K.'s Competition and Markets Authority has opened an investigation into Paramount Skydance's proposed $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, led by David Ellison. The regulatory review will assess whether the deal raises competition concerns in the British market.

The CMA will announce its first-phase decision by a set deadline, determining whether to approve the merger or escalate it for deeper scrutiny. The combined company would rank among the world's largest entertainment conglomerates, uniting substantial film, television, and streaming operations from both organizations.

cards.headline: Idris Elba Says Audiences Would Not Accept Black James Bond
cards.teaser: Actor Idris Elba stated that audiences would not accept a Black actor in the role of James Bond, despite years of speculation about his potential casting.
cards.body:
Rewritten Card:

Idris Elba has dismissed rumors that he was seriously considered for the James Bond role following Daniel Craig's departure. The 53-year-old actor, currently promoting his film Masters of the Universe, told British GQ that speculation about him taking on 007 was "never legit."

Elba also weighed in on broader discussions about the character's future, cautioning against attempts to make James Bond "woke." He suggested the iconic spy should remain true to its original conception rather than undergo significant changes to fit contemporary sensibilities.

cards.headline: Jay-Z Announces Jay-Z 30 Retrospective Concerts in Paris and Los Angeles
cards.teaser: The rapper will perform shows celebrating 30 years of his career in two cities this fall.
cards.body:
Jay-Z and Roc Nation have announced retrospective Jay-Z 30 concerts celebrating three decades of the artist's career. The shows will take place in Paris on September 10, 2026, and Los Angeles on October 23. These performances follow Jay-Z's recent appearance at the Roots Picnic and his upcoming Yankee Stadium shows.

Tickets go on sale June 11 through presales with Citi and Mastercard. The concerts are designed to showcase Jay-Z's influential catalog and impact on hip-hop culture.

cards.headline: Prime Video Releases Trailer for Legally Blonde Prequel Series Elle
cards.teaser: The streaming service will debut all eight episodes of the series following young Elle Woods on July 1.
cards.body:
Prime Video has released the trailer and key art for the first season of Elle, a prequel series to Legally Blonde. All eight episodes will be available on the streaming platform on July 1.

The series follows Elle Woods before her time at Harvard Law School, meeting her in 1995 as she navigates life during a tumultuous period. The show explores the character's earlier years as she transitions from being an L.A. it girl to an outcast in Seattle.

cards.headline: Scary Movie Reboot Tops U.K. and Ireland Box Office
cards.teaser: The Paramount franchise revival earned $5.6 million in its opening weekend across the region.
cards.body:
Paramount's Scary Movie reboot claimed the top position at the U.K. and Ireland box office with a debut of £4.1 million ($5.6 million). The franchise revival navigated a highly competitive marketplace to secure the leading spot.

The Amazing Digital Circus: The Last Act from Piece Of Magic Entertainment opened in second place with $3.6 million, while Masters Of The followed in third. The box office faced incoming competition from Steven Spielberg's Disclosure Day.

hero.headline: Trump says Iran peace deal could be reached within days
hero.body:
President Trump announced he could approve an Iran peace deal on Friday that would require major concessions from Tehran, including opening the strait of Hormuz and eliminating the country's nuclear programme. However, top Iranian officials disputed his claims, signalling that no final agreement had been reached.

Trump spent more than two hours in the White House situation room with senior aides before making his announcement. On his Truth Social platform, he outlined the terms he said Iran must accept: never developing nuclear weapons, opening the strait of Hormuz to all traffic without tolls, removing mines from the waterway, and allowing the US to collect and destroy highly enriched uranium from an Iranian nuclear site. Trump also said he would lift the US naval blockade against Iran, though it remained unclear whether this would be contingent on the agreement being confirmed.

The list of demands presented by Trump as a completed agreement would indicate Iran had capitulated on key positions, including its historical right to collect tolls from ships using the strait, the release of frozen assets, and its insistence on maintaining its nuclear programme.

Iranian officials quickly rejected Trump's characterisation of the negotiations. The semi-official Tasnim news agency reported that no final understanding had been reached and described Trump's post as "in line with his usual pattern of making unilateral and egotistical statements." Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei told state media that "exchanges of messages are continuing, but no final agreement has been reached yet."

Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said discussions about the strait of Hormuz had focused on management "in line with our sovereign responsibilities and international law," suggesting Iran would not accept Trump's proposed terms. Iran's Fars news agency characterised Trump's announcement as a "mixture of truth and lies" that did not reflect actual negotiations.

A White House official confirmed the situation room meeting had lasted approximately two hours but did not announce a deal. The official stated: "President Trump will only make a deal that is good for America and satisfies his red lines. Iran can never possess a nuclear weapon."

Iran's top negotiator Mohammad-Bagher Ghalibaf sent a defiant message, declaring that Iran had "no trust in guarantees or words, only actions are the measure." He suggested Iran was prepared to resume fighting if talks failed to extend the ceasefire and end the war.

A meeting in Washington between US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Pakistan's Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, who serves as a key mediator, ended without public comment on the negotiations. Trump reportedly needed more time to decide whether to accept a negotiated agreement that would defer difficult issues, including the fate of Iran's remaining nuclear material stockpile, into subsequent negotiations.

cards.headline: Vance refers Walz, Ellison to Justice Department for fraud investigation
cards.teaser: Vice President Vance will refer Minnesota Gov. Tim Walz and Attorney General Keith Ellison to the Justice Department following a House Oversight Committee report.
cards.body:
Vice President Vance announced late Monday that he will refer Minnesota Gov. Tim Walz and Attorney General Keith Ellison to the Justice Department for a criminal fraud investigation. The referral stems from findings in a House Oversight Committee report.

The report alleges that Walz and Ellison were aware of widespread fraud and government failures. The specific nature of the alleged fraud and the timeframe covered by the investigation were not detailed in the announcement.

cards.headline: House to vote on $69.5 billion spending bill for immigration enforcement
cards.teaser: The House is set to take up a budget reconciliation bill to fund immigration enforcement as Congress faces deadlines on surveillance powers and spending priorities.
cards.body:
House Speaker Mike Johnson and GOP leaders will brief reporters Tuesday morning as Congress works to pass key legislative priorities before upcoming deadlines. The House is preparing to vote on a $69.5 billion budget reconciliation bill focused on immigration enforcement.

Congress also faces pressure to pass a long-term extension of warrantless spying powers under the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act. The dual legislative push comes as lawmakers juggle multiple time-sensitive items with significant policy implications.

cards.headline: House holds hearing on Southern Poverty Law Center after Justice Department investigation
cards.teaser: The House Judiciary Committee convenes a hearing on the civil rights group months after the Trump administration accused it of funneling money to extremist groups.
cards.body:
The House Judiciary Committee is holding a hearing Tuesday on the Southern Poverty Law Center following accusations from the Trump administration that the civil rights organization funneled money to extremist groups. The SPLC announced in April that it was under investigation by the Justice Department.

In May, the organization pleaded not guilty to charges related to using a nonprofit structure to support extremist activities. The hearing occurs as Congress examines the group's finances and operations during the federal investigation.

cards.headline: Trump criticizes federal judge for striking down H-1B visa fee
cards.teaser: President Trump criticized a federal judge who blocked his proclamation imposing a $100,000 fee for H-1B visa applications.
cards.body:
President Trump criticized a federal judge on Tuesday for striking down his proclamation to impose a $100,000 fee on new H-1B visa applications. Trump told reporters the federal courts are creating significant obstacles for his administration's policies.

The administration had proposed the fee as a measure to discourage foreign workers from displacing American jobs. The judge's ruling represents another judicial challenge to the administration's immigration policy initiatives.

cards.headline: Melania Trump honors winners of White House AI challenge for students
cards.teaser: The first lady unveils winners of the administration's first artificial intelligence competition for students at a White House ceremony.
cards.body:
First lady Melania Trump on Tuesday unveiled the winners of the Trump administration's first artificial intelligence competition for students at a White House ceremony. The challenge was announced last August, when the first lady called on students nationwide to showcase American innovation.

The competition encouraged young people to demonstrate their skills in artificial intelligence applications. The ceremony marks the culmination of a months-long program designed to promote technology education among American students.

cards.headline: Deb Haaland wins New Mexico Democratic primary for governor
cards.teaser: The former Biden administration official secured the Democratic nomination and could become the first female Native American governor if elected.
cards.body:
Former Biden administration official Deb Haaland won the Democratic primary for governor in New Mexico on Tuesday. Haaland could make history as the first female Native American governor if she wins the general election.

Haaland previously served in the Biden administration before launching her gubernatorial campaign. She will face the Republican nominee in the general election later this year.
